title: Always started huge projects only to never finish them. Made something much simpler to learn the whole flow. Would love some feedback.
author: OinkLikeAPig
selftext:
So I did some game development 7 years ago at a course through my studies and absolutely loved it. Did apply for some jobs at a few gaming studios, but found my path through elsewhere in IT.

Anyways, I did this game to try the whole flow. Servers, domains, database, Ko-Fi, socials, mails etc., and ended up liking it a lot.  
Showed it to a few friends and family. They liked it too, but can't tell if its biased since they know I am passionated can talk a lot about the topic in general lol.

It's called Wizstrike. It's Counter-Strike-style rounds, but you're a little voxel wizard. You buy spells at the start of each round, and every spell is a skill shot, so you have to aim. It runs in the browser, and bots fill in when there aren't enough players.

Most of the code was written with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. I did the design, testing and decided what should be there and not.

It's far from finished and there's plenty I'm unsure about, so I'd really like to hear what feels off: spell balance, the maps, controls, anything that confused you in the first few minutes.  
Also the tougher feedback as is this just slop, boring etc., really would love any honest feedback.  


[https://wizstrike.com/?ref=reddit](https://wizstrike.com/?ref=reddit)

(PC only, since it's mouse-aimed.)
